links.targetTitle: BD planning — industry and companion-software selection (20 Aug 2026)

title: Powerhouse trades short-term consultancy value for long-term product scalability, and uses the transit to find PMF
content:
The session framed two revenue modes as an explicit trade rather than a sequence to be rushed. Consultancy projects are "high-value" but "not scalable in the long term". Product revenue is "low-value" but "scalable in the long term".

The connecting move is that PMF is established *along the way* — the consultancy work is not merely a bridge that funds the company until the product is ready, it is the mechanism by which the product learns what to be. That reframes each engagement as evidence-gathering with a paying client attached, and it sets a standard for which engagements are worth taking: one that generates revenue but no product learning is a worse deal than its invoice suggests.

The implied risk, not discussed in the session, is that consultancy revenue is comfortable enough to defer the transition indefinitely.
description: Consultancy projects are high-value and unscalable; product revenue is low-value and scalable. The strategy is to earn from the first while establishing product-market fit toward the second.
